subject: Unexpected tenant 429s — quota scope mismatch and remediation
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@orbitalhealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 08:16:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected tenant 429s — quick heads-up and next steps

Hi Sam —

Thanks for flagging the 429 spike this morning. We’re seeing a tenant-scoped quota being applied with the wrong scope tag which reduced the effective window for your embedding calls; that’s producing the transient 429s you reported between ~07:40–08:05 PT.

Immediate actions we’ve taken:
- Put an automated retry card on the route to avoid client-side hard failures.
- Throttled non-critical background workloads on our side for your tenant to free up headroom.
- Opened an investigation (IR-20260815-7543) and attached the current tenant_quota_map snapshot.

As a remediation we propose a config patch that replaces the incorrect quota profile for tenant orbital-health with the intended "standard-embedding" scope. We’d like to schedule a quick config swap (expected <5m impact) — are you available for a 10:00–10:30 PT window today, or do you prefer we do an immediate hotfix now?

I’ll loop Dev and Evelyn in to execute the change and validate. Sorry about the disruption; we’ll follow up with a detailed postmortem and compensation proposal.

— Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Sam Turner <sam.turner@orbitalhealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 08:32:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected tenant 429s — quick heads-up and next steps

Rishi —

Thanks for the quick reply. We saw the 429s in our production logs and a small number of customer-facing requests failed (approx 0.6% of requests during the window). It caused brief retries at the app layer but no persistent data loss.

We’d prefer the hotfix now if it’s safe, otherwise 10:00 PT works. Please confirm if you’ll be rolling back any config or if this will be a targeted mapping update. Also can you include an estimate for any billing credit given the impact window?

— Sam
Director of Platform, Orbital Health
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 08:40:01 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Unexpected tenant 429s — quick heads-up and next steps

Fwding Sam — short plan below. Dev — can you validate the quota map and confirm whether this was a tag-translation bug during a recent rollout? Evelyn — please prepare a candidate credit amount; they reported ~25 minutes of elevated errors (we should reconcile logs).

Key asks:
- Confirm root cause (mapping vs. policy enforcement bug).
- If mapping, apply targeted mapping update for tenant_id: orbital-health (hotfix) with minimal route impact.
- Share config-diff and rollback steps.

I’ll notify Sam once we have ETA.

— Rishi
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 08:52:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Unexpected tenant 429s — quick plan and rollback

Rishi / Evelyn —

Quick diagnosis from the runtime team: when we rolled the new quota-profile sync last night, a migration rule misinterpreted the tenant tag for "orbital-health-prod" and assigned the tenant the lower-throughput "batch-internal" profile instead of "standard-embedding". The mapping table shows the wrong profile_id (profile_83 -> should be profile_12).

Planned remediation (hotfix):
1) Apply mapping patch (config-diff.patch attached) to update the profile_id for tenant orbital-health.
2) Recompute effective windows for active sessions (this is an atomic metadata refresh; tokens in-flight are unaffected).
3) Warm the tenant cache for the embedding route for 60s after the change.

Impact: change is metadata-only, expected <5 minutes of elevated retries only during the cache warm period. We will monitor 429 rates for 30 minutes after.

Rollback: reverse config-diff; we have a tested rollback script in the runbook.

Proceeding now unless you object.

— Dev
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@orbitalhealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:05:12 -0700
Subject: Update: mapping fix applied, verification in progress

Sam —

We applied the targeted mapping fix at 09:02 PT. Dev’s team warmed the cache and monitored the route; 429s returned to baseline within ~3 minutes. Attached is a short snapshot of the tenant_quota_map after the change as well as the config diff we applied.

Root cause summary (short): a tag-translation edge case in the quota sync translated the tenant environment tag incorrectly during last night’s rollout, assigning the lower throughput profile.

Next steps:
- We’ll publish a full postmortem with timeline and corrective actions (deploy guard for quota migrations).
- Evelyn will propose a proportional credit for the 25-minute window of elevated errors and the small customer retry impact.
- We’ll schedule a 30-min follow-up call to walk through the fix and the postmortem.

Links and artifacts: incident record (https://redwood.app/incidents/IR-20260815-7543), snapshot attached (incident-snapshot-logs.tar.gz).

Would you like the follow-up call today at 11:00 PT or Monday morning?

— Rishi
From: Sam Turner <sam.turner@orbitalhealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Orbital Health Platform Team <infra@orbitalhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Aug 2026 17:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Update: mapping fix applied, verification in progress

Rishi —

Thanks for the quick remediation and the explanation. We appreciate the follow-through and the artifacts. 11:00 PT on Monday works for us for a post-incident sync (calendar invite to follow).

Please include the proposed credit and any mitigations you’re putting in place to prevent quota-migration regressions. We’ll want the credit applied to invoice D-10459 and a note in our vendor security log for audit.

— Sam
